title: LP2-00–55: prime-minus-one shifts and known openings
question: Does uninterrupted prime-minus-one arithmetic recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings at the start of an LP2-00–55 page?
summary: 3190 complete candidates, covering 29 starting offsets and both arithmetic directions, yield no exact matches to nine fixed 12-rune openings. Other beginnings and interruption rules remain untested.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Apply prime-minus-one shifts modulo 29, with both subtraction and addition. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known openings; retain full candidates.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–28 inclusive; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 3190 candidates, 28710 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other beginnings, offsets above 28, interruptions, heading removal, reversed input, word or row resets, cross-page carry, other numerical schedules and language scoring.

finding: Zero exact opening matches. Full rerun reproduced every saved candidate; an independent trial-division and inverse-arithmetic check audited all 3190 candidates and the 56-rune LP2-56 control.
limitations: This tests nine specific initial openings, not general readability. Offsets 0–28 do not exhaust a nonrepeating prime sequence. The known LP2-56 interruption is not searched or transferred. Computational review only; human review pending.
next_steps: Declare alternative schedules or boundary rules as separate variants. Specify interruption bounds and plaintext criteria before inspecting results.

family.title: Numerical keystreams and known openings
family.question: Do declared numerical schedules recover fixed known openings under explicit offset and advancement rules?

review.reviewer: Codex — exact rerun, independent candidate audit and known-answer control; human review pending

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12.10, standard library. Independent audit: python experiments/records/lp2-prime-minus-one-openings/check.py

visuals.caption: First four steps of the known LP2-56 control. The experiment tests uninterrupted reuse; this illustration is not a new reading.

browser_followups.title: Try the prime-minus-one stream with three restart rules
browser_followups.question: Do outputs from the fixed prime-minus-one stream resemble the maintained language samples across 29 starting places, both arithmetic directions and page, line or word restarts?
browser_followups.scope_change: Keep the original 29 starting places, addition and subtraction, and LP2-00-55. Include page restarts and add line and word restarts. Compare language samples instead of the nine fixed historical openings.
browser_followups.limitation: Use the stored 305-term sequence once per restart, without wrapping, skipped runes or carry between pages. These new comparisons have no results yet.
